tasks.title: Capture the actual Developer Preview 1 starting state
tasks.goal: Retain the exact source, package and interface baseline from which the authorized implementation starts.
steps: After NEXT-P0-GATE and before any milestone implementation or accounting edit that changes product bytes, resolve the actual source commit/tree and exact repository/worktree scope. Capture this boundary first; the baseline is not automatically b1291b06, an old research tag, the planning commit or a version string.

Retain a raw before-state inventory under evidence/ and a provisional transition.json with DP1 captured, DP2 pending and documentation input pending. Distinguish source truth from measured executable evidence; BASE.2 validates this authored provisional record after creating the registered schema.

Inventory authored sources/specs, lock and recipe identities, package coordinates with exact content hashes and available immutable provider locators, externally sourced captures, CLI/MCP registrations, durable formats, configuration/boot/installation surfaces and supported capability families. Record explicit inclusion and reasoned exclusion sets; a mutable 1.0.0 coordinate alone never identifies a package.

Record artifact digests/provenance only for available measured builds, with toolchain, host/target/platform, applicable commands and actual results. For unavailable artifacts or resources retain the reason and reproduction requirements; preserve the captured source even if later native proof is pending.

Review the capture against the actual Git tree and existing Phase 0 evidence. Retain the product-scope census and account separately for planning/accounting-only files so that adding the capture cannot shift its own baseline.
positive_cases: Two captures of the unchanged selected boundary agree on source/package/content identity.
A package whose bytes changed under 1.0.0 is distinguishable from its old capture.
Missing native artifacts remain explicitly unavailable while source capture is retained.
negative_cases: A current branch name or version string without exact source/content identity cannot close capture.
An untracked product file, nested owned package or external input is not silently omitted.
DP2, publication, freeze or prototype graduation cannot be inferred from writing a release index.
checks: Manual exact-tree and package-capture reconciliation against retained Phase 0 evidence; this is a review, not an existing executable validator.
acceptance: DP1 refers to the actual pre-implementation boundary and each included source/package is exactly identifiable or explicitly unrecoverable with a blocker.
The initial capability/surface denominator and scope exclusions are retained in permanent evidence; no unavailable run is marked passed.
Provisional capture has not been presented as schema-validated before BASE.2.
tasks.safe_stop: Stop after retaining the baseline capture; do not start milestone work until BASE.3 is accepted.
tasks.commit_subject: docs(release): capture the Developer Preview 1 baseline
notes: NEXT-A26 is the temporary design unit supplied by the root packet. Read its accepted permanent replacement after promotion. PROP-068 is PROPOSED until BASE.2 creates it; BASE.1 reads the temporary capture rule and must not claim a missing permanent file exists. Create permanent law before production code or tests cite its anchors.

Only listed outer write roots may change. Proposed paths are not claims of existing files. Narrow configured spec-root change records and documentation paths to the actual accepted binding before dispatch; refine the packet if a necessary path is outside that perimeter.

Permanent release records use immutable change IDs, capability/topic IDs and exact captures, never NEXT task IDs as product identity. The temporary task-to-change bridge is execution evidence and is removed at campaign retirement.

TO CREATE checks name future obligations and must not be reported as existing or passing. BASE.2 defines and tests their exact command grammar; later packets use that accepted grammar. A missing validator, zero selected tests or unavailable platform is an unmet check.

Keep NEXT-EXECUTION-AUTHORITY blocked during planning. These tasks do not authorize public publication, host installation, version bumps, prototype graduation, new IDE clients or an autonomous scheduler.

A clean capture may use a committed tree; any deliberate dirty input requires an exact retained overlay and an explicit source-scope disposition before implementation. Do not erase dirty work to make capture convenient.

Verification follows the current multi-user-planning economy: run required affected checks against exact inputs; mutation testing is optional only for a concrete suspicious signal and a bounded cheaper proof, never a ritual for every contribution.

tasks.title: Define permanent release accounting and deterministic validators
tasks.goal: Create the permanent contract and generated machine-readable formats independently of future change and migration runtimes.
steps: Create PROP-068 as ordinary release/change-accounting law, including the DP1/DP2 identity model, evidence semantics, prototype policy, documentation intake, exact-scope reconciliation and post-retirement proof. Check the proposed filename against the actual tree before minting it.

Place release-impact records at changes/<immutable-id>/release-impact.json under the configured spec root. Define these as ordinary versioned JSON data and non-normative change evidence. Define versioned transition.json, documentation-map.json and validator report/request formats in the existing format registry with canonical schemas, generated bindings/readers and round-trip fixtures.

Define immutable change identity, before/after capture references, affected capability/topic and permanent contract anchors, user impact and documentation impact with separate explicit no-impact reasons, migration action class, evidence, introduced/reverted/superseded relationships and acceptance provenance. Distinguish individual contribution records from net transition conclusions.

Define a permanent read-only checker and deterministic draft assembler under tools/preview-transition/. Establish and document the exact proposed checker grammar: check.py --transition <path> --mode capture|contribution|bindings|documentation|release|retired --format json. Bindings mode requires --stage roles|linked; documentation mode requires --stage intake|updated|verified; release mode requires --stage reviewed|verified. Other modes reject --stage. Each stage validates only its completed obligations and reports later required proof as pending, never passed. Establish assemble.py --transition <path> --output-dir <bound-path>; assembling never accepts work or overwrites reviewed prose without an explicit owned output path.

Use existing schema/codegen entrypoints and generated readers for owned wire formats; no independent handwritten wire parser or duplicate vocabulary. Generate machine reports with exact subject IDs, missing evidence, unavailable/unsupported distinctions and stable ordering, independent of clocks and absolute checkout paths.

Implement semantic cases for stable capture identity, unknown record epochs, malformed references, equivalent no-op transitions, additions/removals, same-version different content, deterministic assembly and preservation of human editorial prose. Validate the provisional BASE.1 capture without rewriting its historical facts.

Define stage predicates and test their boundaries: bindings/roles proves native role adoption and identity preservation, linked additionally proves migration/capability linkage; documentation/intake requires exact supplied capture/binding/topic census, updated additionally requires reviewed topic delta, verified additionally requires actual current build/link/claim proof; release/reviewed requires independent net reconciliation and guidance, verified additionally requires migration rehearsal. Retired mode checks real scaffold absence and all permanent finalization prerequisites; candidate eligibility is distinct from an already recorded final attestation. Missing future proof cannot fail an earlier valid stage or be counted as completed by that success.
positive_cases: A consumer reads the retained formats through generated readers and can enumerate every unresolved migration/documentation obligation.
Deterministic assembly gives identical drafts from identical captures and records in different checkout paths.
An explicit user-no-impact record can still require documentation updates.
negative_cases: Unknown epoch, wrong field type, duplicate immutable ID or dangling capture fails with a machine diagnosis.
Handwritten parsing, clock-derived output changes or a generated draft presented as accepted documentation fails review.
The bootstrap tools must work before M-02 change runtime, M-13 migration runtime and M-16 facade completion.
An intake or reviewed-stage PASS must not imply verified documentation, completed rehearsal or finalized DP2; unsupported mode/stage combinations and omitted required stages refuse.
checks: TO CREATE/USE AFTER BASE.2: python -B -m unittest discover -s tools/preview-transition/tests -p test_*.py
TO CREATE/USE AFTER BASE.2: python -B tools/preview-transition/check.py --transition docs/releases/developer-preview-1-to-2/transition.json --mode capture --format json

CONDITIONAL ORACLE: cargo xtask check-codegen only when the actual diff affects schemas, generators, generated-output registration or a dependent contract. Bind a narrower existing oracle if available; the global command needs that concrete impact and no adequate narrower check.

CONDITIONAL ORACLE: cargo xtask wire-diff only when the actual diff affects wire/format behavior, its corpus or epoch semantics. Bind a narrower existing oracle if available; the global command needs that concrete impact and no adequate narrower check.
acceptance: Permanent laws, registered schemas, generated readers, tested command grammar and meaningful nonzero semantic tests are available before BASE.3.
The bootstrap dependency direction is acyclic: later domain services adopt these records; these tools do not depend on their future implementation.
Schema/codegen work and application behavior are committed separately under PROP-044; generated files are never edited by hand.
tasks.safe_stop: Stop with validated capture and independently usable accounting tools; contribution enforcement remains BASE.3.

tasks.title: Require contribution records before central acceptance
tasks.goal: Make missing release and documentation accounting visible from the first implementation contribution.
steps: Initialize the temporary task-to-change coverage bridge using existing stable task IDs without changing their identity or acceptance state. Treat it as one routing view over permanent change records, not a new task scheduler or a permanent source of release semantics.

Define the central acceptance procedure: every actual contribution commit and out-of-plan repair receives permanent release-impact record(s), or separate reasoned user-no-impact and documentation-no-impact dispositions. One task may map to several changes and several tasks may implement one immutable change; record actual before/after subjects and acceptance provenance.

Require capability/topic membership and permanent source anchors before accepting a claimed effect. Amend the denominator for newly introduced API/configuration/format/installation behavior; finding an unplanned delta expands accounting instead of silently reducing scope.

Implement read-only checks over the selected contribution's exact commit/tree delta and bridge references. Document and invoke the accepted contribution-mode command as an ordinary required step before every central acceptance, recording its exact subject and result; bind any CI hook only in a separately authorized CI task. Preserve candidate evidence across retries and reject stale captures. The central reviewer still decides semantic adequacy; a worker-written record or passing shape check is not acceptance.

Test missing contribution records, missing either no-impact reason, dangling capability/topic IDs, unaccounted new API, duplicate change IDs, one-to-many mappings, explicit reverts/supersedes and metadata-only record maintenance. Keep all milestone first children gated on this accepted foundation through root-owned DAG wiring.
positive_cases: A legitimate internal refactor has distinct supported no-impact reasons and exact commit evidence.
A later corrective contribution joins the same immutable change or an explicit related change without reusing an ID with new meaning.
An unplanned repair is accounted even though it has no original implementation task row.
negative_cases: A task count of 201 or all-green bridge rows cannot prove actual diff coverage.
An omitted new public registration, dangling capability or missing documentation disposition blocks acceptance.
A revert cannot erase the original contribution or be reported as a delivered feature without net reconciliation.
checks: TO CREATE/USE AFTER BASE.2: python -B -m unittest discover -s tools/preview-transition/tests -p test_*.py
TO CREATE/USE AFTER BASE.2: python -B tools/preview-transition/check.py --transition docs/releases/developer-preview-1-to-2/transition.json --mode contribution --format json
acceptance: Every future milestone acceptance has an executable accounting check and a central semantic review obligation tied to actual contributions.
Temporary task references and permanent release facts are explicitly separated and removal of the bridge does not lose change identity.
All nonzero semantic cases pass; the preserved original implementation task contracts remain unchanged.
tasks.safe_stop: Stop after contribution enforcement is accepted; root may dispatch only authorized dependency-ready work.
